source.title: Stored in Optimizer State, Valued by Later Training: A Causal Account of Subliminal Trait Transfer

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests subliminal trait transfer using teacher-generated number data and trait-behavior measurements, but its main intervention and measurement focus on optimizer-state surgery and route-dependent continuation rather than reproducing the original study’s full method and measure.
record.gate_note: The study directly tests transfer from teacher-generated bare-number data and reports behavioral outcomes, state-surgery results, and route-dependent effects. Its optimizer-state prediction-error tables also bear on the proposed mechanism. Results cited from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains Qwen2.5-0.5B and Llama-3.2-1B students on bare-number outputs from trait-biased versus neutral teachers. It reports source-minus-neutral trait responses, so its results bear on A. Its state-surgery tests bear on D (what carries the signal after source removal). Re-evaluations with held-out prompts and observers bear on E. The source exposure is very brief: 4 to 8 updates. The main behavioral readouts are conditioned on later continuations, and the engineered ones are built from the readout direction. This makes it a different method aimed at the claim, not a replication.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially right. The authors add that the distinctive subliminal stage is entry through a compatible teacher–student interface. Downstream transport and valuation, they say, are generic to any gradient-port perturbation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses teacher-generated bare-number data and trait-conditioned teacher outputs, followed by student fine-tuning and trait-related behavioral readouts. The study focuses on gradient-port perturbations, matched source-free route forks, adjoint prediction, and optimizer-state transplantation; its central route design is not simply the original transfer protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: Behavioral sign and magnitude change with the source-free continuation route and observer. The Qwen route topology is reported across four source positions and five traits, with weaker statistical resolution for some traits. On Llama, adjacent contrasts grow from eight to sixteen source-free updates. Costate prediction loses resolution at low source-corpus sizes and is reported as baseline-beating consistently only at and above 1024 rows.

fits_no_version.finding: The transport and optimizer-relay recurrence predicts responses in non-LoRA MNIST MLP/CNN systems with auxiliary-head targets. This is not a subliminal trait-transfer setting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer state (first moment or momentum velocity) relays any gradient-port perturbation into later parameters after the source is removed.

fits_no_version.finding: Tangent and costate predictors reproduce physical descendants and route-mean signs. These are accuracy figures for the study's own method.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A full-trainer-state adjoint predicts the sign of route-conditioned source effects.

record.problems: Several behavioral panels use seven or fewer seeds; some auxiliary comparisons are single-seed or descriptive. The main Qwen route effects depend on engineered continuations, and direct source-control behavioral responses vary by trait and seed. The full-parameter comparison is single-seed. No different-base student comparison is reported.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within the row limit, omitted supplementary outcomes include Qwen source-position contrasts, random-plane controls, route-baseline comparisons, additional generated-choice and observer checks, the remaining transplant-subset rankings and per-seed recovery-error entries, and non-LoRA MNIST physical-transport experiments. These appear in Figures 2-11 and Appendices B, I-N, P-Q; they do not add a distinct test of the claim versions beyond the results recorded.

untested.parts: Code and maths-reasoning outputs as the transfer medium; multi-epoch fine-tuning of the kind used in the original (source exposure here is 4 to 8 updates).
No misalignment or other harmful trait is tested.

Token entanglement, divergence tokens and steering-vector directions are not distinguished experimentally. How the signal enters the gradient is not tested; only its persistence after source removal is.
No LoRA-rank sweep. Full fine-tuning is only a single-seed descriptive control that cannot show trait-specific transfer.

missing.what: Non-subliminal controls. Gradient-sign noise and random gradient give Γ endpoints similar to the owl source (e.g. Γnum +0.534 for owl versus +0.380 and +0.389).

Llama direct source-control responses are weak and seed-heterogeneous: animal −0.012 ± 0.013 (AdamW), −0.005 ± 0.005 (momentum SGD), color +0.016 ± 0.025. The source-cut behavioral response is −0.001 ± 0.026.
missing.locator: Appendix I boundary summaries; Appendix M.6

missing.what: Llama generated-choice and free-generation readouts stay at the noise floor at both horizons.
Behavioral-vector recovery by w+m: SSE/ZERO 0.0017–0.0079, beating w, m and w+v in 9/9 cells. Oak m-only response is +0.00612 versus +0.01518 for full state.
The momentum-SGD factorial reproduces the route ordering in 3/3 seeds (Holm p = 0.25, descriptive). The velocity-only transplant is released by later updates.
TinyLlama shows no stable behavioral sign, with 62–84% cancellation. A SmolLM2 cell shows 90.9% cancellation and a different dominant slot pair.

record.verdict_notes: The record's version labels V1/V4/V5 correspond to A/D/E. The source windows are only 4 to 8 updates on about 128–1831 rows, much shorter than the original fine-tuning. The engineered S± routes use the readout direction, so the signs on those routes are partly by construction. The proposed carrier concerns persistence after the signal enters the gradient, not which data features carry it. Single-author preprint.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not report code outputs or maths-reasoning data as the transfer medium. The main owl results are route-conditioned effects, not a uniform increase in owl preference under every continuation.
No comparison tests a student with a different base model against a same-base student.
No harmful or misalignment trait is tested.

The paper tests optimizer-state transport and route-dependent behavioral valuation, but does not experimentally distinguish the claim’s listed token-entanglement, divergence-token, or steering-vector mechanisms.
The study does not sweep LoRA ranks. Its full-parameter comparison is a single-seed descriptive control, not a broad robustness evaluation.
No prompt-only insertion of linked tokens without fine-tuning is tested.
